lessons.title: Acute Ischemic Stroke 2026: EMS triage, TNK, thrombectomy & time windows
lessons.summary: 2026 AHA/ASA guideline updates the full stroke pathway from prehospital evaluation through acute treatment, with broader thrombectomy eligibility and stronger systems-of-care emphasis.

sections.title: 1) Prehospital recognition
paragraphs: Use validated stroke recognition, establish last known well, glucose, anticoagulant history, baseline function and rapid destination decision. BE-FAST helps capture posterior symptoms but should not replace local stroke scale/pathway.

sections.title: 2) Time & imaging
paragraphs: Do not delay transport for unnecessary interventions. In-hospital imaging determines hemorrhage, LVO and thrombolysis/thrombectomy eligibility; prehospital notification helps shorten door-to-treatment times.

sections.title: 3) 2026 thrombolysis update
paragraphs: For eligible adults within 4.5 h, 2026 guideline recommends tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg. Extended-window thrombolysis may be reasonable in selected patients based on advanced imaging.

sections.title: 4) Thrombectomy expansion
paragraphs: Eligibility for EVT has broadened, including selected larger-core and posterior circulation/basilar occlusions, with recommendations extending to up to 24 h in defined populations.

sections.title: 5) Supportive care
paragraphs: Avoid hypoglycemia; treat severe abnormalities, monitor oxygenation/BP per stroke protocol, and avoid treatment that delays reperfusion.

quick_review: Do not delay definitive stroke pathway

research_updates.title: Major guideline update
research_updates.takeaway: 2026 AIS guidance endorses mobile stroke units, refines EMS triage, expands tenecteplase use and broadens EVT eligibility including basilar occlusion and selected larger-core patients.

research_updates.title: AHA/ASA 2026 expands stroke systems and treatment eligibility
research_updates.takeaway: The 2026 guideline adds recommendations around mobile stroke units, refined EMS destination strategy, broader tenecteplase and EVT eligibility, and pediatric AIS.

quiz.q: 2026 AIS guideline recognizes which thrombolytic option within 4.5 h in eligible adults?
quiz.explain: The 2026 guideline recommends either TNK 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg in eligible adults.

lessons.title: Seizure, Status Epilepticus & Altered Mental Status
lessons.summary: ชักเป็น symptom ไม่ใช่ diagnosis. EMS ต้อง prioritize safety/ABC, duration, glucose, pregnancy/toxin/trauma, temperature and persistent altered state.

sections.title: 1) Seizure priorities
paragraphs: Protect from injury, position/suction airway as needed, monitor ventilation/oxygenation, obtain glucose and time the seizure. Do not restrain forcefully or place objects in the mouth.

sections.title: 2) Status / ongoing seizure
paragraphs: Persistent convulsive seizure is time-sensitive because longer duration increases treatment resistance and metabolic complications. Benzodiazepine route/dose must follow local protocol and available access.

sections.title: 3) Differential
paragraphs: Hypoglycemia, stroke/ICH, infection, eclampsia, toxin/withdrawal, electrolyte disturbance, trauma and psychogenic nonepileptic events are important differentials.

sections.title: 4) Post-ictal reassessment
paragraphs: Repeat neuro exam, vitals, glucose, trauma check and transport decision. Failure to regain expected mental status raises concern for nonconvulsive status, structural lesion or ongoing toxic/metabolic problem.

key_points: Persistent altered mental status needs reassessment

quiz.q: Early bedside test in altered/seizing patient?
quiz.explain: Hypoglycemia is rapidly reversible and must be checked early.

lessons.title: Thunderclap Headache & Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
lessons.summary: “Worst headache” ไม่ใช่ criterion เดียว—onset speed, neurologic findings and context matter.

sections.title: 1) Thunderclap phenotype
paragraphs: Pain reaching maximal intensity within seconds to about a minute is a major red flag. SAH, reversible cerebral vasoconstriction, cervical artery dissection, venous thrombosis and pituitary apoplexy are important causes.

sections.title: 2) SAH clues
paragraphs: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, neck stiffness, syncope, seizure, focal deficit or reduced consciousness. Sentinel headaches may precede major hemorrhage.

sections.title: 3) Assessment
paragraphs: ABC, GCS, pupils, focal neuro exam, glucose, anticoagulants, pregnancy/postpartum, onset time. Avoid dismissing normal initial neuro exam.

sections.title: 4) Prehospital care
paragraphs: Manage airway/ventilation when needed, treat seizures, avoid hypotension/hypoxemia and transport to imaging/neurosurgical capability based on system.

lessons.title: Meningitis & Encephalitis: Infection of CNS
lessons.summary: ไข้ + altered mental status/meningismus/seizure ต้องคิด CNS infection แม้ triad ไม่ครบ.

sections.title: 1) Syndromes
paragraphs: Meningitis primarily involves meninges; encephalitis involves brain parenchyma and more often causes altered behavior, focal deficits or seizures. Mixed presentations occur.

sections.title: 2) Do not require the classic triad
paragraphs: Fever, neck stiffness and altered mental status are not all present in every patient. Elderly, immunocompromised and children may be atypical.

sections.title: 3) Immediate threats
paragraphs: Airway compromise, status epilepticus, shock, raised intracranial pressure and severe sepsis.

sections.title: 4) Prehospital priorities
paragraphs: Isolation/PPE when indicated, ABC support, glucose, seizure control per protocol, hemodynamic support and early hospital notification. Definitive antimicrobial/antiviral timing is hospital/protocol dependent.

lessons.title: Acute Spinal Cord Syndromes & Neurogenic Shock
lessons.summary: แยก cord injury, spinal shock และ neurogenic shock ซึ่งไม่ใช่สิ่งเดียวกัน.

sections.title: 1) Cord syndromes
paragraphs: Motor/sensory deficit, sensory level, autonomic dysfunction and bladder symptoms suggest cord pathology. Trauma, epidural compression/abscess/hematoma and vascular causes are time-sensitive.

sections.title: 2) Neurogenic shock
paragraphs: Loss of sympathetic tone after high spinal cord injury can cause hypotension with relative bradycardia and warm vasodilated skin. Hemorrhage must still be excluded first in trauma.

sections.title: 3) Spinal shock
paragraphs: Neurologic phenomenon of transient loss of reflexes/flaccidity below cord lesion—not a hemodynamic shock state.

sections.title: 4) EMS priorities
paragraphs: Spinal motion restriction when indicated, maintain oxygenation/perfusion, serial neuro exam and destination appropriate to trauma/neurosurgical needs.

pitfalls: Attributing trauma hypotension to neurogenic shock before excluding bleeding

lessons.title: Acute Dizziness/Vertigo: Do Not Miss Posterior Stroke
lessons.summary: คำว่า “เวียนหัว” กว้างมาก ต้องแยก syndrome และ neurologic danger signs.

sections.title: 1) Define the syndrome
paragraphs: Distinguish acute vestibular syndrome (continuous vertigo/nausea/gait unsteadiness), episodic triggered vertigo and spontaneous episodic dizziness. Symptom quality alone is unreliable.

sections.title: 2) Posterior circulation danger
paragraphs: New severe gait/truncal ataxia, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, focal weakness/numbness, new headache/neck pain or vascular risk raises concern for central cause.

sections.title: 3) HINTS caution
paragraphs: HINTS can be powerful in correctly selected continuous acute vestibular syndrome when performed by trained clinicians; misuse outside that context can mislead.

sections.title: 4) Prehospital focus
paragraphs: Check glucose, neuro exam, gait if safe, LKW/onset and consider stroke pathway rather than labeling “peripheral vertigo” too early.
